title: Bug: PMON missing access to necessary devices for platform monitoring post privilege removal
author: gregoryboudreau
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

PMON container no longer has access to the full set of device nodes under /dev/, which is breaking PMON services that need to, for example, open I2C device files (e.g., /dev/i2c-*). This appears to be a side effect of removing --privileged (https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/a13685f3081dfd6c11f1995917a9390de352c8fd) , since that previously granted broad device access; without it, the container only sees whatever devices are explicitly passed through. Some vendors have worked around this by adding targeted --device mappings, but that approach doesn’t cover the full set of I2C devices (or other /dev nodes PMON may need) and becomes fragile as platforms vary and device nodes change.

This change has been addressed piece-meal by multiple vendors across multiple device types, but still lacks the necessary extensive coverage:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/bd0e6c34476377efecf61f18834a8a613da273c4
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/736606a288fcf29da4a3f5a3a3404ce028e7172b
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/259ed3b182de1826c596cf8f272d1ae9b75fb0c6
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/b251c0d2bb5d02993d3d5e1983a6c7d50e58412d

### Steps to Reproduce

Any direct `i2c` access (excluding i2c-0 which was explicitly added and through sysfs) will fail. Example is on Cisco platforms, we attempt to retrieve a status word from PSUs via `i2cget` which will fail because the PMON container cannot access targeted pmbus for the PSU.

comments.body: @gregoryboudreau Previously there was a PR https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24250 to resolve the issue on /dev/i2c-0 missing. If you add /dev/i2c-* on your platform, will it resolve this issue?

comments.author: gregoryboudreau
comments.body:
> [@gregoryboudreau](https://github.com/gregoryboudreau) Previously there was a PR [#24250](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24250) to resolve the issue on /dev/i2c-0 missing. If you add /dev/i2c-* on your platform, will it resolve this issue?

That is one method but also introduces a race condition, when we iterate over the /dev/i2c-* instances during the docker create we won't get new i2c instances when they are created after the fact. Beyond that, we get into the idea of providing access to all devices to the platform monitor service which is the approach I prefer (don't see a real reason to limit PMON on this front, let me know if there's some security concern). 

One AI from the chassis call was to see if we could just mount /dev/ in the docker, need to dig a little deeper on how docker manages these permissions.

That is up to vendors, say for example you have a FRUable device like PSUs or fans, how the switch handles that, whether it tears down the i2c devices, etc., is fully up to the vendor, the point I was trying to make is that by iterating over and using --device for allowing device access, we run into a condition where PMON _can_ be unable to access real devices that get added or modified after the fact of the docker's creation.

comments.author: Staphylo
comments.body:
I second @gregoryboudreau 's point of view here.
`pmon` is a platform management targeted container and should therefore have access to the exact same view of the hardware as the host has.

I proposed further mitigations to the removal of the `--privileged` flag in following PR which added some missing devices to pmon https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24463/ 
While it temporarily solves the problem for our use case it likely doesn't solve other vendor's nor our future use cases.
This list of devices to mount in `pmon` will keep growing and will not be shrinkable at the risk of breaking some platform support.
This `pmon` limitation is bound to hit vendors again in the future.

As pointed out above, everything dynamic is a problem, I would also like chassis cards (linecards, fabric) to the list.
Same goes for `udev` rules that some vendors might chose to implement or rely on. Their result is not replicated in the container.

I recently came across another issue related to the availability of the debugfs in the pmon container.
Some driver expose some of their information via this filesystem, but it's no longer available in pmon.

Having a cat-and-mouse game on `pmon`'s availability of hardware resources is I think detrimental to platform support efforts.

comments.author: gregoryboudreau
comments.body: I am trying out some changes locally to mount the /dev/ directory directly along with providing broad device-cgroup-rule to the pmon container to see if that could work without previously mentioned race condition. The big question with any approach is what are the security implications that initially brought about this `--privileged` flag removal, we likely want the _minimal_ amount of permissions that allows PMON functionality without above-mentioned cat-and-mouse dynamic.

linkedPullRequests.title: pmon: tolerate /dev reordering and bus hot-plug
linkedPullRequests.author: ashwnsri
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Aimed at #25142

pmon runs against a fixed --device list captured at 'docker create', which breaks in two ways: a block-device partition (e.g. sda1) named in kernel probe order can disappear after a disk reorder and fail 'docker start', and a bus node that appears after create (i2c/cpld/fpga/ipmi/uio/spidev/gpiochip/mtd) is denied and invisible to the container.

#### How I did it

Pass reorder-invariant whole disks, pre-authorize the hot-plug device classes, and keep the container's /dev in sync at runtime. The change is strictly narrower than --privileged.

files/build_templates/docker_image_ctl.j2
  - get_pmon_device_mounts(): skip block-device partitions and pass the reorder-invariant whole disk instead.
  - get_pmon_device_cgroup_rules() (new): emit 'c <major>:* rwm' for each hot-pluggable bus class so a sibling created after 'docker create' (e.g. an i2c bus behind a mux on optic insert) is already permitted.
  - start(): pass those rules as --device-cgroup-rule on docker create.
  - postStartAction(): call pmon-dev-bridge.sh resync to converge /dev.

files/image_config/pmon/pmon-dev-bridge.sh (new)
  - Helper that mirrors allowed character bus nodes into the running pmon container(s): 'resync' converges every allowed node on start; 'event add|remove' handles a single udev hot-plug event via mknod/rm.

files/image_config/udev/rules.d/99-pmon-dev-bridge.rules (new)
  - udev rule forwarding add/remove uevents to pmon-dev-bridge.sh so the container's device view tracks hot-plug after creation.

files/build_templates/sonic_debian_extension.j2
  - Install pmon-dev-bridge.sh to /usr/local/bin (mode 755) at image build time.

#### How to verify it

All checks are read-only except the dynamic-bridge demonstration, which is **container-only
and fully reversible** — the host `/dev` is never modified. Run on a device built from /
flashed with this fix. 

Results: [pmon-how-to-verify-it.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28871000/pmon-how-to-verify-it.md).

[PMON-HOTPLUG-TEST-REPORT.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29029346/PMON-HOTPLUG-TEST-REPORT.md)
